clue.text: The Right Stuff and Top Gun aged badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the preceding words come out jumbled

blocks.note: the film title plus the next word, taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film critic sneers that two classic aviation movies have dated poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Right Stuff and Top Gun look like a pair of film titles, but the first is the definition and the second is anagram material, split by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the right stuff is having the drive and energetic vigour that the idiom get-up-and-go also describes.

clue.text: Travel over most of large desert

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept
in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second in the column

blocks.note: to travel is to go
large means big

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the bulk of a vast desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert stretching across Mongolia and northern China, so it is an example of a desert.

clue.text: Cut a dash, to some extent – voilà!

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the preceding words is used, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of cut, the word a, and the start of dash

explanation.surface: Someone shows off with a flourish and announces their reveal like a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations made when presenting something with a flourish, like a conjuror revealing a trick.

clue.text: Breakfast items stolen, for example case of grapefruits

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: poached means stolen, especially game taken illegally
the usual abbreviation for for example
the outermost letters of grapefruits

explanation.surface: A list of breakfast-table things that went missing, with grapefruits offered as one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs cooked gently in simmering water are a standard morning dish, so they are items served at breakfast.

clue.text: Less socially adept, demanding more energy, not right

indicators.note: not here marks that one letter is swapped for another, so the word is kept but with a different letter in one spot

blocks.note: needier means more demanding
E is the physics symbol for energy
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone awkward in company is also more needy and somehow off.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of the word for more demanding becomes an R: the energy and right letters trade places in the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is stereotypically awkward among people, so the comparative describes someone with weaker social skills.

clue.text: King George and Queen Elizabeth: that’s even more majestic

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A royal couple together are said to be more majestic still.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal cyphers on postboxes give GR and ER; joined by the plain word and they build the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means imposing and stately, so the comparative form is more imposing, more stately.

clue.text: What to say to a horse while holding on anxiously, primarily?

definitions.text: What to say to a horse while holding on anxiously, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily points to what comes first, so the initial letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A nervous rider clings on and wonders what command will stop the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the traditional command to a horse to stop or slow down, shouted by a rider clinging on in alarm.

clue.text: That man’s little musical group, iconic, not half theatrical

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped, here its first three of six letters

blocks.note: belonging to that man is his
a trio is a small band of three players
taken as written before losing half

explanation.surface: A fan describes a man's small band as iconic, though only partly so, and rather showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is melodramatic and overacted, like a performance on stage, so it means theatrical.

clue.text: Crime that I arranged, being calculating

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the preceding letters are reordered

blocks.note: these three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A villain confesses to having planned an offence, being a scheming sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Calculating looks like the scheming adjective but is used in its literal sense of working with numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the working out of sums with numbers, which is the activity of calculating, read as a noun.

clue.text: Period during which you might have an unpleasant shock?

definitions.text: Period during which you might have an unpleasant shock?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nasty surprise or fright at some time
setter's reading: a shock is a thick mass of hair, here an untidy one

explanation.walkthrough: Shock is read as a sudden fright, but it also means a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a day when your hair will not behave, and by extension a day when everything goes wrong.

clue.text: For starters, alcoholic sparkling tincture, Italian

definitions.text: For starters, alcoholic sparkling tincture, Italian

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An aperitif is described: something boozy, fizzy and Italian to begin a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sweet fizzy white wine from Piedmont in northern Italy, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Singer confused bride with shrug in church

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the two words are scrambled
in places the jumbled letters inside the short word for church

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters, joined by with
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: At a wedding, a bewildered bride shrugs at the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris de Burgh is the Irish singer-songwriter best known for the 1986 hit The Lady in Red.

clue.text: Naïve types accepting president’s to get rid of weapons

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to bin something is to throw it away
Abe, short for Abraham Lincoln, plus the 's
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Innocent idealists welcome a presidential plan to disarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president; the possessive 's stays on his name and goes inside the word for throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: Babes in arms are infants still carried, so figuratively the phrase means inexperienced, innocent people.

clue.text: In the manner of Royal Marine, punch time-keeper

blocks.note: à la is French for in the style of
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine
to clock someone is slang for hitting them

explanation.surface: A soldier from the Royal Marines lands a blow on a timekeeper, perhaps a referee.
explanation.walkthrough: Clock as a verb is British slang for to punch.
explanation.definitionFit: This device keeps the time and rings at a set hour to wake a sleeper, a clock with a bell.

clue.text: Spies entrap idiot, minor poet regularly following stars

indicators.note: to entrap is to hold something inside, so the spies' letters surround the rest
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
following places the selected letters after the word for idiot

blocks.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
an ass is a fool
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Secret agents set a trap for a fool and a lesser poet who chase celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars looks like the celebrities a minor poet follows, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a constellation, a W-shaped group of stars in the northern sky named after a mythical queen.

clue.text: Tragic Greek figure, skinny, next to the German

indicators.note: next to says the two pieces sit side by side in order

blocks.note: lean means thin
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A thin character from Greek tragedy stands beside a German.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero and drowned in a storm, a doomed hero.

clue.text: Drugs dipped in caviar for Brat Pack actor

indicators.note: something dipped in goes inside, so the first piece is placed within the second

blocks.note: caviar is fish roe
blow is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Cocaine sprinkled into caviar is the extravagance of a 1980s young Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Lowe starred in St Elmo's Fire, a core member of the 1980s group of young film actors nicknamed the Brat Pack.

clue.text: Once again, accepts contract’s terms and quits

blocks.note: first meaning: signs a contract a second time
second meaning: gives up a job or post

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are opposites: a player who re-signs stays, one who resigns leaves; only a hyphen separates them.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-signing renews an agreement, while resigning means stepping down from employment; the spelling is shared.

clue.text: ‘River Dee rising,’ son first exaggerated

indicators.note: first moves the letter for son to the front of the other pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the Exe is a river in Devon
dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
rising means going up

explanation.surface: A report that a river is flooding, with a son's claim the first to be overstated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a real river, which makes River Dee read as one name; here Dee is the letter D, and the Exe is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex up a report is to make it sound more dramatic than the facts warrant, overstating its claims.

clue.text: ‘Pescatarian option’? Ham is doubly out of order!

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word is written twice

explanation.surface: A diner objects that ham on a fish-eater's menu is doubly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is thin slices of raw fish, so it suits a diet that excludes meat but allows seafood.

clue.text: During autopsy, MP to manipulate evidence

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters are found inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of autopsy through MP and to into manipulate

explanation.surface: A politician tampers with the evidence at a post-mortem.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign that indicates an illness or problem, so it is a piece of evidence for it.

clue.text: Interrogate corrupt cronies about Congress in the morning

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are pulled out of shape
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the other pieces

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
congress can mean sexual intercourse
am is short for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: An investigator questions crooked associates over an early-morning political scandal in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature, but here it means sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross-examine is to question a witness closely, typically one called by the other side in court.

clue.text: Blue European nobleman?

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Is a risqué continental aristocrat being described?
explanation.walkthrough: Blue also means smutty, which fits the Marquis, whose writings gave us the word sadism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Sade was a French aristocrat of the eighteenth century, a titled nobleman and notorious author.

clue.text: Stinging insects, with tip of wings clipped, remain poisonous creatures

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
clipped means cut off, so that letter is removed from the insects

blocks.note: wasps are insects with stings
the first letter of wings

explanation.surface: Insects with damaged wings are still able to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes of the Nile region, the kind Cleopatra used, so they are poisonous animals.

clue.text: Poet, retiring lone wolf at heart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the letters are found in the middle of the phrase
retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the central letters, from the end of lone into the start of wolf

explanation.surface: A shy poet is at heart a solitary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen was the English poet of the First World War who wrote Dulce et Decorum Est.

clue.text: Real idiots misconstrued views of the Observer, etc

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly interpreted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fools misread a newspaper's opinion pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, not a person watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials are articles giving a newspaper's own opinions, as published by papers like the Observer.

clue.text: Middle section taken from Muslim holy book: it’s a Buddhist riddle

indicators.note: taken from means removed, and middle section says it is the central letter that goes

blocks.note: the Koran is the holy book of Islam

explanation.surface: A passage lifted from the Quran turns out to be a Zen puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A koan is a paradoxical question used in Zen Buddhism to provoke insight, like the sound of one hand clapping.

clue.text: Sympathisers omitting greeting disturbed intelligence chiefs

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so a word's letters are removed
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Supporters who skip the hello unsettle the heads of the secret service.
explanation.definitionFit: Spymasters run networks of agents, so they are the people in charge of espionage and secret information gathering.
